confirmed: The journal abstract explicitly distinguishes 9,198 humans from 215,542 LLM observations; it does not report people randomized, exclusions, or counts for individual outcomes (Europe PMC PMID 41436597, abstract sentence 2).

The ai_vs_human context classification and core = no are supported by the designs described: separate human and LLM output comparisons, followed by manipulations of models. No randomized study assigning people AI assistance was identified (journal abstract; PsyArXiv draft pp. 4-11, Results, and pp. 14-15, Methods). This does not constitute a full-text audit of the journal version.

All four quoted reported findings match the journal abstract, allowing for whitespace: slightly higher human mean creativity, greater human variability and upper-tail creativity, persona/role performance rising to a threshold, and mixed-to-negative strategic prompting results (Europe PMC PMID 41436597, abstract sentences 4-6).

The one_line_finding reproduces the journal abstract headline counts and qualitative results; no numerical effect sizes, confidence intervals, or pooled estimates are provided there (Europe PMC PMID 41436597, complete abstract).
This is original comparative research, not a synthesis; the empty synthesis fields are appropriate (journal abstract; PsyArXiv draft pp. 4-11, Results).

The older PDF names the Divergent Association Task, asks for 10 single-word nouns, and describes an automated semantic-distance score. This supports divergent_test for that draft, but its measurement details have not been verified in the journal full text (PsyArXiv draft p. 3 and pp. 14-15, DAT score computation).

The older draft references supplementary tables, including Tables S5-S8, and provides https://osf.io/a9v2t for both data and code. All 27 PDF pages were read; the referenced supplementary information is not included (PsyArXiv draft p. 5 and p. 16, Data Availability and Code Availability).

The journal metadata supports online publication on 2025-12-23 and volume 10, issue 3, pages 531-540; Europe PMC dates the issue March 2026 (Crossref DOI 10.1038/s41562-025-02331-1, published-online/volume/issue/page; Europe PMC journalInfo).
summary: The context classification, headline counts, and abstract findings are supported, with no randomized study assigning people AI assistance identified. Four corrections concern source provenance, model counts assigned to individual outcomes, comparison coding, and unverified company involvement; the journal full text remains unavailable.
